agent_summary:
Tested all 5 WSTG-IDNT items against the OWASP Juice Shop host juice.lab.test using the idnt1/idnt2/busl1/busl2 test accounts and ~121 requests (reads plus pre-approved writes on my own accounts). All items marked done.

Key findings (leads recorded):
- CRITICAL — Privilege escalation via registration (IDNT-01/03): anonymous POST /api/Users with "role":"admin" returned 201 and created user id 42 with role admin (confirmed by /api/Users?sort=-id). No server-side role whitelisting; accounts are isActive:true immediately with no email verification. Roles in use: customer, admin, deluxe, accounting.
- MEDIUM — Account enumeration (IDNT-04): GET /rest/user/security-question?email= returns the question for a registered email but {} for unknown; duplicate-email registration returns 400 vs 201; and product reviews, /api/Feedbacks and /rest/memories leak author emails unauthenticated. Login (401) does NOT differentiate, so login is not an oracle.
- MEDIUM — Weak account recovery (IDNT-02): POST /rest/user/reset-password resets a password with only email+security-answer (wrong answer=401, correct=200), no second factor/rate-limit token, and the question is enumerable.
- LOW — Weak username policy (IDNT-05): usernames are non-unique (idnt1 and idnt2 both set to "idntshared9"); username supplied at registration is ignored; markup username is dropped (some char validation).
- Notes/info: GET /dataerasure 500 leaks build path; OAuth client config + jwt.pub exposed; /api/BasketItems and /api/Quantitys readable by customers (authz overlap).

Positive observations: role escalation on an existing account via PUT /api/Users/:id is blocked (401, record unchanged); /api/Addresss/:id and /api/Cards/:id enforce ownership (400). But /api/Users/:id and authentication-details/api/Users list leak the full user table (incl. password hashes, totpSecret) to any authenticated customer and ids are sequential — reproduced across idnt1, idnt2, busl1, confirming trivial full-base enumeration (overlaps authz lanes 87/88/89/90, not re-led).

Not tested: JWT/token forgery and SSO redirect abuse (token never visible to me; belongs to session/config lanes); 2FA enroll/verify and account-deletion writes were out of scope for read-only identity checks. No brute force or credential guessing performed. Several file/directory-exposure observations overlap existing info/conf/errh leads and were not duplicated.

leads.title: [agent] /api/BasketItems returns data to a user with an empty basket (possible BOLA)

detail.text: GET /api/BasketItems as customer idnt1 (id 27, whose own basket is empty) returned HTTP 200 with a 1045-byte JSON body (exchange x73), suggesting the generic BasketItems collection is not scoped to the caller's basket and may expose other users' basket line items. For the authorization lane to validate field-level content (body not shown here due to display budget).

leads.title: [agent] Account enumeration via /rest/user/security-question and registration duplicate-email response

detail.text: Unauthenticated GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<addr> returns the user's security question object (200, {"question":{..."Mother's maiden name?"...}}) when the email belongs to an account that has a security answer set, but returns an empty body ({}) for an unknown email — allowing an anonymous attacker to enumerate which email addresses are registered. Separately, POST /api/Users with an already-registered email returns HTTP 400 while a new email returns 201, a second enumeration oracle. Note the whole user table (emails included) is also directly readable via GET /api/Users and /rest/user/authentication-details by any authenticated customer (separate authz leads), so enumeration is trivially possible.

leads.title: [agent] Identity/token config exposed unauthenticated: Google OAuth client config and JWT public key

detail.text: GET /rest/admin/application-configuration (no auth, exchange x61) returns the app config including googleOauth.clientId (1005568560502-6hm16lef8oh46hr2d98vf2ohlnj4nfhq.apps.googleusercontent.com) and the full authorizedRedirects list used for SSO login. GET /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (x62) returns the RSA public key used to verify session JWTs. These disclose the identity/authentication configuration; combined with the separately-reported /ftp backup exposure (hardcoded JWT signing material), token-forgery / SSO-redirect abuse against the identity layer should be assessed. Overlaps config/info lanes; flagged here for its identity-management impact.

leads.title: [agent] Public registration (POST /api/Users) honors client-supplied role=admin — privilege escalation

detail.text: Unauthenticated POST /api/Users with body including "role":"admin" returned HTTP 201 and created user id 42 with role "admin" (profileImage defaultAdmin.png), confirmed by GET /api/Users?sort=-id showing id 42 createdAt 2026-10-16T20:18:33 role "admin" — matching the registration timestamp. The registration API performs no server-side role whitelisting, so any anonymous user can self-provision an administrator account. Account was created isActive:true with no email verification step. Four roles exist in the system: customer, admin, deluxe, accounting.

GET /dataerasure (authenticated as idnt1) returned HTTP 500 with body "Error: No answer found!" and a server build path "/juice-shop/build/routes/dataErasure.js:74:23". The GDPR data-erasure route leaks internal file paths in its error. Belongs to the error-handling/info-disclosure lane; noted here because it is part of the account-management surface.

leads.title: [agent] Weak account-recovery: password reset relies only on an enumerable security question + answer

detail.text: POST /rest/user/reset-password resets a user's password given only {email, answer, new, repeat}: a wrong answer returned 401 and the correct answer (for my test account id 45) returned 200 and set a new password, with no authentication, no email-link confirmation, and no additional factor. The matching security question is disclosed unauthenticated by GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<addr> (returns the question for a known email, {} for unknown), and the full set of 14 canned questions is at /api/Users? -> /api/SecurityQuestions. Combined, an attacker who can guess/know a victim's security answer (chosen from weak canned questions) can take over the account. No rate-limiting token or captcha was required on the reset request observed.

leads.title: [agent] Weak username policy: non-unique usernames; username ignored at registration

detail.text: POST /profile username=idntshared9 as idnt1 (id 27) and again as idnt2 (id 28) both succeeded (302); GET /api/Users/27 and /api/Users/28 confirm both accounts now carry the identical username "idntshared9" — the application enforces no username uniqueness. Separately, supplying a username in the POST /api/Users registration body was ignored (stored ""), and a markup username () set via /profile did not persist (some character validation drops it). Net: usernames are non-unique and cannot be relied on as an identity, enabling impersonation/confusion.
